name: get_customer
description:
Look up a customer's ACCOUNT PROFILE: name, email, phone, mailing address, loyalty tier, and account standing.

Input format: {"customer_id": "CUST-<digits>"} (e.g. "CUST-40912") or {"email": "person@example.com"}. Accepts a customer ID or an email address; it does NOT accept an order number.

Example query: "What email do we have on file for account CUST-40912?" or "Is this customer's account in good standing?"

Edge cases: If more than one account matches an email, it returns multiple matches, ask the customer for their customer ID to disambiguate rather than guessing. It returns an empty result (not an error) when no account matches.

Use this when the question is about WHO the customer is, their profile, contact information, or account standing, and not when the question is about a specific order's status, contents, or shipment (use lookup_order for that).

name: lookup_order
description:
Retrieve a single ORDER's status and contents: order status, line items, totals, shipment tracking number, and delivery dates.

Input format: {"order_id": "ORD-<digits>"} (e.g. "ORD-88213"). Accepts an order number only; it does NOT accept a customer ID or email address.

Example query: "Where is my order #88213?" or "What items were in order ORD-88213 and has it shipped yet?"

Edge cases: It returns an empty result (not an error) when the order number does not exist. A cancelled order still returns its record with status "cancelled". It does not return other orders belonging to the same customer.

Use this when the question is about a SPECIFIC order, its status, items, or shipment, and not when the question is about the customer's profile or listing all of their orders (use get_customer for account-level questions).

name: extract_data_points
description:
Extract specific STRUCTURED FIELD VALUES from a document (dates, amounts, names, IDs, line items) and return them as JSON.

Input format: {"document": "<full document text>", "fields": ["invoice_number", "total_amount", "due_date"]}. `fields` names the exact data points to pull.

Example query: "Pull the invoice number, total, and due date from this invoice."

Edge cases: When a requested field is absent from the document, return null for that field rather than fabricating a value.

Use this when you need discrete field values out of a document, and not when you need a prose summary (use summarize_content) or a yes/no check of a claim (use verify_claim_against_source).

name: summarize_content
description:
Produce a concise NATURAL-LANGUAGE SUMMARY of a document's main points.

Input format: {"document": "<full document text>", "max_words": 150}.

Example query: "Give me a two-paragraph summary of this contract."

Edge cases: For very long documents, summarize section by section; do not silently drop the middle.

Use this when you need a human-readable overview of what a document says, and not when you need specific field values (use extract_data_points) or to confirm one statement (use verify_claim_against_source).

name: verify_claim_against_source
description:
Check whether a SPECIFIC CLAIM is supported, contradicted, or unaddressed by a source document, returning a verdict plus the supporting excerpt.

Input format: {"document": "<full document text>", "claim": "The contract auto-renews annually."}.

Example query: "Does this contract actually say it auto-renews?"

Edge cases: If the document neither supports nor contradicts the claim, return "unsupported" rather than guessing.

Use this when you need to confirm or refute one statement against a source, and not when you need to extract fields (use extract_data_points) or summarize the whole document (use summarize_content).

name: extract_web_results
description:
Extract the relevant RESULTS FROM WEB CONTENT (a web search response or a fetched web page): titles, URLs, snippets, and publication dates, returned as structured entries.

Input format: {"query": "<original search query>", "page_or_results": "<raw search results or fetched page content>"}.

Example query: "From these search results, pull the top 5 article titles, links, and dates."

Edge cases: Skip ads and navigation chrome; return an empty list when the page has no substantive results.

Use this when the source is web content (search results or a fetched page), and not when the source is an internal document (use extract_data_points or summarize_content instead).
